fix: validate categories and mileage in restored backups

## Why

Restore from Backup checks contacts, visits, time entries, plans, preferences, profile and the pet before it writes anything. Categories and mileage were the exception: they went straight from the file into the stores. A damaged or hand-edited file, such as one where `categories` isn't a list or a trip is `null`, saved that bad data to the device. Home reads the categories on every launch (`categories.find` in `serviceReportCategory.ts`), so one bad file could crash the app every time it opens, and the bad records synced on to the user's other devices.

## What

- `normalizeBackupFile` now passes `categoryStore` and `mileageStore` through the same `parsePayload` call as the other stores, and the restore writes the parsed lists.
- A file whose category or mileage lists aren't lists is rejected, and nothing changes, as with contacts today.
- An unreadable record (`null`, missing fields, a non-numeric distance) is dropped and the rest of the list is kept.
- As before, only the stores and lists the file holds are restored. A file without mileage, or without one of its lists, leaves the device's own alone.

## Screenshots

No UI change.

## Verification

- `pnpm vitest run src/app/sync/__tests__/backupRecovery.test.ts`: 16 passed. Two of the new tests fail on main: `categories: { a: 1 }` / `trips: 'x'` is now rejected without touching local data, and `null`/invalid categories, vehicles and trips are dropped while valid ones restore. A third test checks that mileage lists missing from the file are left alone.
- `pnpm vitest run src/app/sync src/lib/petBackup.test.ts`: 43 files, 464 tests pass. `pnpm run typecheck` and eslint/prettier on the changed files pass. The commit and push hooks ran lint and the full suite.
- Not run on a device: the change is in the restore data layer and is covered by unit tests.

benchmarks.task_description:
fix: keep custom field values in older backups

## Why

Restoring a JSON backup made before custom fields got stable ids (spring 2026) brings back every contact, but their custom field values (Language, Floor, and so on) never show. Those files key each value by its label and keep the label list in `customContactFields`. The restore drops that list as an unknown preference, and the one-time boot migration that converts labels to ids has already run on the device, so the values come back with no definition pointing at them. They sit hidden on the contact, and the user thinks they're gone.

## What

- `restoreBackupFile` now converts a legacy file's contacts (active and archived) with the same `migrateCustomFieldsToIds` the boot migration uses, when the file's preferences hold `customContactFields` and its contact store has no `customFieldDefs`.
- Each legacy label goes to the device's own definition when one has that id (or legacy alias) or the same active label; otherwise it gets a new definition after the device's own. The device's existing definitions are kept.
- Current files (with `customFieldDefs`) restore exactly as before.

## Screenshots

No UI change.

## Verification

- `pnpm vitest run src/app/sync/__tests__/backupRecovery.test.ts`: 17 passed. The two new tests for a legacy file (values land under a `Language` definition; local definitions survive) fail on main. Two more cover reusing a same-label local definition and leaving a current file alone.
- `pnpm run typecheck`, eslint and prettier on the changed files pass; the commit and push hooks ran lint and the full test suite.
- Not run on a device: the change is in the restore data layer and is covered by unit tests.
- Out of scope: legacy `serviceReportTags` aren't turned into Categories on restore; entries still show their tag name through the `report.tag` fallback.

fix: show this week on home for older installs

## Why

This Week was added to Home in April 2026 (9ad9633f), but no preferences migration came with it. Hydration merges shallowly, so an install that had already saved a `homeScreenElements` map kept its old map, and that map has no `thisWeek` key. Home read the missing key as hidden (`!homeScreenElements.thisWeek`), while Settings → Home sections reads a missing key as shown (`?? true`).

As a result, everyone who had used the app before April never saw This Week on Home. Settings told them it was on, and turning it on there did nothing because it already showed as on.

## What

- Home hides This Week only when the user explicitly turned it off (`=== false`), the same check Mileage, Pet and Did You Know already use. This also covers a map synced from a device on an older build.
- Preferences v12 → v13 adds `thisWeek: true` to a saved map that lacks the key. If the user turned it off, it stays off, and the sync timestamp is left untouched. This reuses the same helper as the v11 → v12 Pet migration, which now shares it.

## Screenshots

Home with a visibility map saved before This Week existed (made-up data; other sections were turned off to keep the screen short).

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| ![Before: no This Week](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/cef43b26-8821-4f74-a54f-09d50860c29d) | ![After: This Week shows](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/4f1d58ca-3f55-4f27-9367-2dd87071d0a6) |

## Verification

- `pnpm vitest run src/__tests__/preferencesPersistMigration.test.ts`: 64 tests pass. The new v12 → v13 tests fail on `main`. I updated the existing v11 → v12 expectations because the chain now also adds `thisWeek`.
- `pnpm run typecheck` and eslint pass. The commit and push hooks ran lint and the full test suite.
- **iOS (WW Verify iPhone 1, `wwv up --platform ios --seed pioneer`):** I set `homeScreenElements` to a map without `thisWeek` and remounted. On `main`, Home showed no This Week. With the fix, This Week appears between the Mileage prompt and the Timer. `wwv errors` showed no errors.
- **Not tested on a device:** the migration itself, which is covered by unit tests. Android was not run either, because the change is shared JavaScript with no layout change.

fix: delete time entries without changing the previous state

## Why

`deleteServiceReport` made a shallow copy of `serviceReports`, then wrote to the year bucket it still shared with the previous state (`reports[year][month] = …` / `delete reports[year][month]`). Deleting a time entry therefore changed the previous state in place:

- Anything holding the old year object (memoized values, subscribers comparing `serviceReports[year]`) saw the entry disappear underneath it, or saw no change at all.
- That can leave stale totals or rows on screen after a delete.
- The store's state history stops matching what was actually written.

## What

The year bucket is now copied before the month is replaced or removed, as `updateServiceReport` already does. `deleteRolloverPair` and `deleteServiceYearReports` already rebuild every bucket, so they didn't need the change.

## Screenshots

fix: stamp erased householder records with the sync clock

## Why

"Erase all householder data" stamps every redacted tombstone with `Date.now()`. Edits are stamped with the calibrated sync clock (`syncTimestamp`), which adds the server offset. When the device clock runs behind the server, a contact edited shortly before the erase has an `updatedAt` later than its tombstone. A peer that still holds the active (or full archived) copy then wins the last-writer-wins merge, and the erased householder comes back on every device. The user asked for this data to be gone, and it shouldn't come back.

## What

Each tombstone is now stamped with `syncTimestamp(record.updatedAt)`, the same way `deleteContacts` and `removeDeletedContact` stamp theirs. That makes every tombstone strictly newer than the record it erases.

No UI change.

fix: keep earlier dates when editing all dates of a plan

## Why

Editing a Recurring Plan from one of its later dates and saving with **All dates in this plan** moved the plan's start to the date being edited. Every earlier date disappeared from the Schedule, the day sheets and the month's planned total. A publisher who had a weekly plan since January and changed its title on next Tuesday's date lost every week from January until then. The data stayed gone after the save, and nothing in the app warned about it.

This came in with the plan form rewrite (d87079c2). The form opens on the tapped date, so its Date pill holds that date, and the "All dates" branch saved that pill value as the plan's `startDate`.

## What

- `allEventsStartDate` in `src/features/plans/lib/planDayDates.ts` works out the start date an "All dates" save keeps. It is the plan's existing start, moved by the number of days the user moved the edited date. If the user doesn't move the date, the start stays the same. If they move this Wednesday to Thursday, the whole series moves to Thursday, as it did before.
- `PlanDayForm` uses it for the "All dates" save. "Only this date" and "This and future dates" are unchanged.
- Unit tests cover the helper, including a daylight-saving week, and a store test checks that the earlier weekly dates still appear after the edit.

A weekly plan that started Oct 7 (made-up data). Its Oct 28 date was edited, and the edit was saved for all dates.

fix(navigator): keep the focused list row rendered so Tab reaches the list

## What & why

Once the focused row in the Messages panel's list mode scrolls far out of view, the keyboard can no longer reach a row. This PR applies the outline's fix from #632 (turn outline) to list mode, as that PR's body proposed: "A follow-up can apply the same one-line `rangeExtractor` to list mode."

The list uses a roving `tabIndex`: the focused row holds `tabIndex=0`, and every other row holds -1. The virtualizer unmounts rows outside its visible range and 5 rows of overscan. When the focused row leaves that range, no row in the list is in the tab order. In Edge, Tab from the filter box then lands on the list's scrolling container. Enter does nothing there, and the arrow keys no longer move between rows, because those handlers sit on the rows.

The fix is one virtualizer option in `MessageNavigator.tsx`: a `rangeExtractor` that always includes the focused index. It reuses `includeIndex` from `outline/rovingFocus.ts`, which the outline already uses and which already has unit tests. The focused row renders at its own offset, so nothing else in the layout moves.

Refs #598

### The test change

The accessibility test's virtualizer mock rendered every row, so no test could see this gap. The mock can now render a narrow window through the component's own range extractor, as the real virtualizer does. Every existing test still renders every row. The new test puts the focused row, the 20th of 20, outside a two-row window. It failed before the fix, with 2 rows rendered and none holding `tabIndex=0`, and it passes after.

### A second follow-up builds on this branch

List mode also places rows at estimated heights, which leaves uneven gaps between them (up to 21.5 px in a 399 px panel). I have a fix ready that measures each row, as the outline does. ## What & why

Z Code stores the assistant model as camelCase `modelId`, but the Z Code provider parser only looked for the opencode-style `modelID`. Every parsed assistant message therefore carried an empty model, and the viewer drops the entire message-details row — model name, token usage, estimated cost and duration — when the model is empty (`src/components/messageRenderer/AssistantMessageDetails.tsx:37-39`). Token counts consequently never appeared on Z Code messages.

This PR reads `modelId` first and falls back to the legacy `modelID` spelling, and covers both spellings with regression tests.

Upstream evidence — zai-org/ZCode @ `3c5b227649371507ddc4eb46ac5133afe6db1cab`:

- The persisted assistant-message contract declares the field as `modelId`, with `providerId` beside it — not `modelID`:
  https://github.com/zai-org/ZCode/blob/3c5b227649371507ddc4eb46ac5133afe6db1cab/apps/zcode-cli/packages/contracts/src/interfaces/session-store.port.ts#L400-L401

fix(scripts): open invitation features on the seeded local stack

Invitation features (`legal-lists`, `list-verification`, `ai-memory`, `activity-timeline`) are admitted only through `API_FEATURE_ACCESS_GRANTS`, which `apps/api/.env.example` leaves at `{}`. A fresh checkout's seeded stack (`bun run agent:up`) therefore showed none of them to the seeded organization.

## Change

- `apps/api/scripts/lib/seeded-organization-grants.ts`: `withSeededOrganizationGrants` returns the configured grants plus an organization grant to the seeded organization (`DEFAULT_ORG_ID`) for every `invitation` feature in `FEATURE_REGISTRY`. A newly registered invitation feature is covered without editing a list.
- `apps/api/scripts/grant-seeded-organization-features.ts`: a dev-only preload that calls `requireLocalDevOpen` before importing anything environment-owning, then installs the merged grants on `envFeatureAccess`.
- `packages/scripts/src/dev-runner.ts`: a seeded stack's API server gets this preload after `register-mock-ai.ts`. Unseeded `bun run dev` is unchanged.

## Why here

The grant decision itself (`feature-access` policy and snapshot) stays untouched: it already reads grants from one object, and it must keep hiding invitation features from organizations without a grant. Grants reach a process from its launcher, as in the e2e stack (`seed-e2e-feature-access.ts` plus `setup-e2e-stack`), so the seeded stack's launcher supplies them. The preload lives next to `seed-utils.ts`, which owns the seeded organization id. The dev runner cannot import the API registry, and a seed-written file would race the server, because the seed runs while the API boots.

Strictly local:

- The preload refuses unless local development access is open.
- `envFeatureAccess` is frozen outside open mode.
- Only the dev runner's seeded stack loads the preload. The e2e stack, which starts `src/server.ts` directly and expects the seeded test user to see no lists, never loads it.

Configured grants are merged, never replaced.

## Tests

- `apps/api/scripts/grant-seeded-organization-features.test.ts`:

  - configured grants stay alongside the seeded grant;
  - in a spawned `NODE_ENV=development STELLA_LOCAL_DEV=1` process, the preload installs the merged grants;
  - in a spawned process without a local `NODE_ENV`, with or without the opt-in, the preload refuses.
- `packages/scripts/src/dev-runner.test.ts`: only a seeded stack's API server carries the preload, and the preload path exists in `apps/api`.
